messages:
jules: quick q — before we expose a WarmStart API on the loader surface, do we want to let customers opt into partial-shard reads + validation hooks, or keep that internal?
maya: +1 to discussing. main worry is safety: user code could call WarmStart on a checkpoint that hasn't finished integrity checks.
arpan: we also need to consider perf: exposing incremental-read means we can't always assume atomicity, which harms the runtime's ability to do fast path mmap/zero-copy.
sasha: fwiw, i'd prefer a small explicit opt-in flag (e.g. allow_partial_warmstart) rather than a public multi-method surface. keeps defaults safe. :thumbsup:
jules: what about a compromise — expose a single WarmStart API but require a Policy object that includes validation level (none/metadata-only/strict) and a runtime flag to opt into fast-paths?
maya: that could work. Policy object needs stable serialization (protobuf/JSON) otherwise we break backward compat. also document semantics around races.
arpan: implications for sharding: if a shard is streaming in and WarmStart hands back a handle to tensors, those tensors must either be immutable or reference-counted with copy-on-write. Otherwise we get data races when we later overwrite the backing buffer.
sasha: can we just return readonly mapped views for partial shards and only create writable copies when the shard is fully hydrated? that's what many apps expect.
arpan: readonly views are fine, but watch for Guest VMs with different mmap semantics. we need an abstraction layer.
jules: good point. infra-bot: deploy-check results: loader-internal-tests passed, integration tests failing on two platforms (arm64 alpine).
maya: arm64 failure is the mmap fallback path — it's lazy and triggers once we change flags. i'll open a follow-up.
sasha: one more UX concern: if we expose validation hooks, users will run expensive checks in prod. maybe we should provide a light-weight checksum cache token that indicates recent validation and can be attested by the system.
arpan: agree. A signed validation-ticket from the registry would let the client trust a checkpoint without local full-verify.
jules: nailed it. plan proposal: (1) WarmStart API that accepts Policy + optional validation_ticket, (2) default policy is strict (server-validated), (3) allow_partial_warmstart flag only when validation_ticket present, (4) runtime implements readonly mmap views + COW on write, (5) document mmap semantics + platform caveats.
maya: sounds good. can we add telemetry hooks so we can measure how often partial warmstart is used and OOMs triggered?
sasha: yes — add per-request tag and quota gating.
arpan: me: will draft an RFC addendum that includes sequence diagrams, the ticket format (signed JSON), and the COW policy. will ping infra for arm64 fallout.
jules: awesome — thanks. i'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to go over API shapes and have the eng-api folks sign off.
infra-bot: reminder: please attach the arm64 integration logs to the RFC PR for triage.
jules: thanks everyone. follow-up: RFC PR number will be posted in this thread when created.
